walkthroughs.body_html:
In Victorian Britain most men still could not vote, and no woman could vote in general elections.

Women slowly won other rights — to own property, to go to university, to keep wages. But many people still believed women should stay at home.

By the 1890s women had had enough. Two main groups grew up to demand suffrage (the vote). 👩‍🦰

The NUWSS (National Union of Women's Suffrage Societies) was founded in 1897, led by Millicent Fawcett.

Members were called Suffragists. They wanted to win the vote peacefully by:

  • Sending huge petitions to Parliament
  • Holding meetings, marches and lectures
  • Writing to MPs

They were patient — but progress was very slow.

In 1903, Emmeline Pankhurst and her daughters Christabel and Sylvia set up the WSPU in Manchester.

Members were called Suffragettes. Their motto was 'Deeds, not words'. They used more dramatic tactics:

  • Chaining themselves to railings
  • Smashing windows
  • Heckling politicians

The two groups disagreed about tactics — but both wanted the same goal. 💜💚⚪
